title: Electorate of Hesse
capsule: The Electorate of Hesse (Kurhessen) was created in 1803 when the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss elevated the Landgraviate of Hesse-Kassel to an electorate, making it anomalously the sole electorate within the German Confederation after the Holy Roman Empire dissolved in 1806. Napoleon annexed it in 1807, incorporating it into the Kingdom of Westphalia under his brother Jérôme; it was restored in 1814 under Elector William I. The electorate sided with Austria in the 1866 Austro-Prussian War; Prussian troops occupied Kassel on 20 June 1866, and the territory was annexed as part of the Prussian Province of Hesse-Nassau by the Treaty of Prague, extinguishing the electorate.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well documented through the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss and subsequent German Confederation acts; they remained essentially stable from 1815 until annexation in 1866.
